title: Volume of rectangular and triangular prisms

draft.title: Volume of prisms
card: Volume is the amount of space inside a solid. It is measured in cubic units, such as cm³.
A right prism has the same cross-section all the way along its length. Volume = area of cross-section × length.
The cross-section is a rectangle, so volume = length × width × height.
The cross-section is a triangle. Example: triangle area 6 cm² and length 10 cm gives volume 6 × 10 = 60 cm³.
draft.remember: Volume of a right prism is cross-section area times length, in cubic units.

a.q: A box is 5 cm long, 4 cm wide and 3 cm high. What is its volume?
a.why: Volume = 5 × 4 × 3 = 60 cm³. Adding the lengths to get 12 is a common mistake, but volume needs multiplying.

b.q: A tent is a triangular prism. Its triangular end has area 2 m² and the tent is 3 m long. What is its volume?
b.why: The end is the cross-section, so volume = 2 × 3 = 6 m³. Adding 2 and 3 gives 5, which is not how volume works.
b.clue: The triangle's area is already worked out.
